 Second Bail Application No. 12 of 2023
Mukesh Sharma ........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent
Present:-
 Mr. Rajat Mittal, Advocate for the applicant.
 Mr. V.S. Rathore, A.G.A. for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Applicant Mukesh Sharma is in judicial custody in Fir No.174 of 2022, under Sections 376, 354,506
Ipc, Police Station Dalanwala, District- Dehradun.

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He has sought his release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
Learned counsel for the applicant appeared through video conferencing.
3. This is the second bail application.
The first bail application being BA1 No.,1805 of 2022, was rejected on 27.09.2022.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the victim has not supported the prosecution case at trial; in fact, her brother and sister have also not supported the prosecution case; the victim has stated that, in fact, the FIR was lodged against one Mahesh and not against Mukesh; she did not identify the applicant at trial.
5. State, despite opportunity, did not opt to file the objections.
6. Learned State Counsel would submit that, in fact, the applicant is the real accused.
He introduced himself as Mahesh to the victim.
It is submitted that it has been discussed in the bail rejection order of the trial court.
7. Be it as it may.
At Para 4 of the first bail rejection order dated 27.09.2022, the Court has recorded the arguments made on behalf of the applicant.
At that time, it was not argued that the applicant is not Mahesh.
He is not an accused.

At that time, it was argued that, in fact, the applicant and the Mukesh Sharma vs State Of Uttarakhand on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87400253/
1 victim were friends.

entities.text: Mukesh Sharma vs State Of Uttarakhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But now, it a change of stance.
Does it mean that the defence is taking advantage of the weakness of the prosecution?
Does it mean that the victim and other witnesses have been won over by the defence?
This Court cannot speculate.

Prosecution may have still opportunity to prove its case, but the fact remains that the victim, after rejection of the first bail application, did not identify the applicant in the Court, as the accused against whom, according to her, she lodged the FIR.

8. Having considered, this Court is of the view that it is a case fit for bail and the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
9.
The second bail application is allowed.
10. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
(Ravindra Maithani, J.) Vacation Judge 20.01.2023
